introHeading: Wedding photo booths for Staten Island's biggest receptions
introParas: Staten Island weddings are famously well-attended, and the island's catering halls are built for it — grand ballrooms near St. George that seat several hundred, waterfront venues around Great Kills Harbor, estate-style properties on Todt Hill where ceremony and reception share the same grounds. We plan every Staten Island booking around that guest count from the start rather than treating every wedding the same size.

The mirror booth remains the right base choice for most Staten Island receptions — full-length format, works for the flower girl and the grandparents alike, which matters at the multigenerational guest lists common across the island. Past roughly 150 guests, routine at the bigger St. George and Great Kills halls, we usually pair it with a roaming attendant so seated tables get covered directly instead of everyone funneling into one line all night. For a younger New Dorp or Tottenville crowd who will post the clip before the band's second set, the 360 booth tends to see the heaviest use.

On logistics: we carry a $3 million policy and turn a certificate of insurance around the same day you give us your venue's contact — standard for the catering halls that dominate Staten Island wedding venues. We arrive an hour ahead and set up in about 20 minutes, in a 10ft x 10ft footprint where the room allows it or 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance where it's tighter. Staten Island is within our standard service area; any bridge toll is built into your quote up front, so there's nothing to discover on the invoice.

faqHeading: Wedding Photo Booth on Staten Island — FAQ

faqs.q: How many hours should we book for a Staten Island wedding?
faqs.a: Three to four hours covers most receptions, though larger St. George and Great Kills ballroom weddings sometimes run longer. Send us your guest count and run sheet and we'll suggest a start time and whether a second attendant makes sense before we quote you extra hours.

faqs.q: Our guest list is large — can one booth keep up?
faqs.a: Past about 150 guests, which is routine at Staten Island's bigger ballrooms, we usually suggest pairing your static booth with a roaming attendant. That way seated tables get covered directly instead of everyone lining up at one station all night.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee to Staten Island?
faqs.a: No surprise fees beyond the standard bridge toll, which is already built into the quote we send from your venue's ZIP code — St. George, Todt Hill, Great Kills, New Dorp and Tottenville are all regular territory for us.

faqs.q: Which booth works best for a Staten Island wedding?
faqs.a: The mirror booth is the safest choice for the family-heavy, multigenerational guest lists common at the island's ballroom receptions. For a younger New Dorp or Tottenville crowd, the 360 booth gets used the hardest.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the booth need?
faqs.a: Optimal is a 10ft x 10ft footprint, with 8ft x 8ft and 7.5ft of ceiling clearance as the minimum — usually not an issue in Staten Island's grand ballrooms, but worth checking if your venue is a smaller estate space. We also need a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet, not shared with the DJ.

About 20 minutes once we're in the room. We build in a full hour ahead of your scheduled start so everything is tested before your first guest walks in. If you need us on site earlier than that, idle time is $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Can you send our venue a certificate of insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million policy and turn COIs around the same day you send us your venue's contact — standard practice for the catering halls most Staten Island weddings are held at.

faqs.q: Do we get every photo from the night, not just the prints?
faqs.a: Yes. Every image lands in an online gallery you can download in full and share with guests, on top of the unlimited prints handed out on the night.

faqs.q: Our ballroom has another wedding right before ours — how does load-in work?
faqs.a: We call the venue's coordinator ahead of time and lock in a specific load-in window, rather than just showing up at your ceremony start time and hoping there's room. St. George and Great Kills halls in particular book back-to-back Saturday weddings, so the turnaround between events is often under an hour — worth confirming before the day, not during it.

faqs.q: How will out-of-town guests get to our Staten Island venue?
faqs.a: The Staten Island Ferry runs free from Lower Manhattan to St. George, useful for guests coming from that side. Drivers from Brooklyn or New Jersey usually come across the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge. Tell us your venue and we can help you figure out the easiest route to include on your invitations.
